title: Zangarmarsh
body: Zangarmarsh is a vast wetland in western Outland, where mushrooms taller than any tree rise over still pools and glowing fungi light the gloom. Sporebats drift overhead, and the giants that wade through the bogs are themselves made of living fungus. When the druids of the Cenarion Expedition arrived, they expected to find only small pockets of life and instead found a thriving wilderness. Then they noticed that the water was falling. The naga of Lady Vashj have raised steam pumps on the great lakes and are draining them into Coilfang Reservoir beneath Serpent Lake, and the marsh has begun to wither. Others share the land: the draenei of Telredor and the Kurenai of the Orebor Harborage, the Darkspear trolls of Zabra'jin and Swamprat Post, the peaceful sporelings of Sporeggar, savage tribes of Lost Ones, and the Ango'rosh ogres, who are cutting down the mushroom forests of the north.

title: Cenarion Refuge
body: The Cenarion Refuge stands in the east of the marsh, at the end of the road from Hellfire Peninsula, and is the headquarters of the Cenarion Expedition. Its leader, Ysiel Windsinger, keeps watch from a balcony behind the inn, while Warden Hamoot and his wardens guard against the naga, who have attacked the druids since the day they arrived. Two great ancients, Ashyen, an Ancient of Lore, and Keleth, an Ancient of War, stand among the buildings and bless those the Expedition trusts. Lauranna Thar'well catalogues the marsh's plants, the Broken refugee Ikeyen teaches the druids what he knows of the land, and Morthis Whisperwing waits for a worthy apprentice while his two birds, Rook and Corvax, circle overhead.

title: Umbrafen Lake and Darkcrest Shore
body: Umbrafen Lake lies southwest of the Cenarion Refuge, and it was here that the Expedition first went looking for the cause of the falling water. What it found on Darkcrest Shore was a steam pump worked by the naga, drawing the lake away. Darkcrest slavers and sorceresses guard the works and drive Dreghood Broken as drudges, and the pump's overseer threatens intruders with the wrath of Warlord Kalithresh. The lake itself is home to Umbrafen eels, whose meat is a staple of the draenei at Telredor, and to mire hydras, whose thick scales resist the damp of the marsh.

title: Umbrafen Village
body: South of the Cenarion Refuge lies Umbrafen Village, home of the Umbrafen, a tribe of Lost Ones who took the side of the naga. The Broken who escaped them call the Umbrafen the worst of all the traitor tribes: their oracles, seers and witchdoctors use dark magic to trap and enslave others, and they are especially cruel to slaves who flee. Their leader is Kataru. Those taken here are not easily freed. The druid Kayra Longmane was seized by a band of them while gathering herbs nearby, and Ikeyen of the Refuge still fears that they will come for him.

title: Funggor Cavern
body: Funggor Cavern opens in the far south of the marsh, near the border with Nagrand and south of Umbrafen Village. It is the home of the sporeloks, who have lately been overrun by marsh dredgers and marsh lurkers that have invaded their caves. The Expedition sent watchers to study the cavern, but had to recall them after repeated attacks by the marsh beasts, and Warden Hamoot believes that killing their leader, Lord Klaq, would put an end to it. The Broken Ikeyen hid here after escaping the Umbrafen, only to flee again when the beasts and spore men fought over the cave, leaving behind everything he owned.

title: Telredor
body: Telredor is built atop a giant mushroom in the east of the marsh, its halls lit by cultivated fulgor spores, since little in the swamp will burn. For centuries it was a secluded retreat for draenei priests and pilgrims who seldom saw visitors. When the orcs began attacking the draenei, refugees arrived in growing numbers, and Anchorite Ahuurn and the other priests turned the shrine into a haven to which many owe their lives. Today it is the Alliance's stronghold in the marsh. Vindicator Idaar watches over the land, Noraani and Haalrun, once its only outsiders, help feed the newcomers, and a dwarf of the Explorers' League has come to settle a score with a giant wasp.

title: The Dead Mire
body: The Dead Mire, northeast of Telredor, was once a lake like the others and a spawning ground for the fungal giants. Its water is gone, and the soil is so dry that the creatures living on it are suffering terribly. The withered giants that remain have been driven mad by the pain and attack anything in their path, and they can no longer spore. Parched hydras and withered bog lords roam the cracked ground, threshalisks lie in the mud playing dead before they charge, and pieces of steam pumps lie scattered about. A troll scout sent from Swamprat Post to explore the mire was found dead beside his spilled inkwell, struck down by a withered giant.

title: Swamprat Post
body: Swamprat Post is the Horde's newest outpost in the marsh, raised by Darkspear trolls just south of the Dead Mire. Shadow Hunter Denjai sent Zurai there with a small band of builders and warriors to give the Horde a presence on the eastern border, after the Alliance began fortifying old draenei ruins, and to tighten the Horde's hold on the roads in and out of the marsh. Marshfang rippers are everywhere, mail armor soon fails in the damp, and the cook answers every complaint of hunger by handing over an axe and pointing at a mushroom. Meanwhile Reavij pines for Magasha, Magasha has eyes only for Zurai, and the witch doctor's charms have done nothing to change that.

title: Feralfen Village
body: Feralfen Village lies in the south central marsh, home of the Feralfen, said to be the most powerful tribe of Lost Ones in Zangarmarsh and keepers of potent medicine. Their mystics, hunters and druids have turned to the worship of animal spirits, and the idols and totems they carve show a serpent and a bird. The bird is a puzzle, since no birds are native to the marsh, and the draenei of Telredor wonder whether the tribe once met the arakkoa. Just north of the village roams Blacksting, a giant bog wasp that drove off the first Explorers' League party to camp there.

title: Boha'mu Ruins
body: The Boha'mu Ruins are the remains of a draenei temple southwest of Telredor, one of several shrines once kept by a small order of anchorites and vindicators. Contact with its keepers was lost during the orcs' war on the draenei, and the Feralfen Lost Ones have since made the ruins their own, as if they remember something of their heritage. Their elder, Kuruti, calls it his temple and wants no visitors in it. The tribe's spirits guard it too. When a Darkspear seer tried to summon the Feralfen serpent spirit at the foot of the temple stairs, the spirit came, and it attacked.

title: The Lagoon and Darkcrest Enclave
body: The Lagoon lies in the south central marsh, a broad stretch of water haunted by lagoon eels, mire hydras and lagoon walkers, among them a great one called Marsh Baron Brok. On its shore stands the Darkcrest Enclave, where the naga run another of their steam pumps. Darkcrest taskmasters and sirens keep Dreghood Broken at the work, and the enclave answers to Rajah Haghazed, leader of the Darkcrest naga. The Cenarion Expedition has tied the Darkcrest to many attacks on its people, and a bounty posted at the Refuge warns that the rajah is extremely dangerous.

title: Cenarion Watchpost
body: The Cenarion Watchpost is a small camp in the southwest of the marsh, west of Quagg Ridge, where Watcher Leesa'oh studies the sporelings and bog lords. She believes that all things in nature are bound in one web, and that anyone who interferes without understanding it will surely cause destruction, so she prefers to watch quietly and take notes. Her fellow druids call her a bit studious. She is never alone: her big cat, Buddy, shares the camp and likes to scratch now and then, though she insists he is only a lovable kitty.

title: Quagg Ridge
body: Quagg Ridge, east of the Cenarion Watchpost, is the land of the bog lords and fungal giants, towering creatures of living fungus. Many of them are starving. Lately they have been crossing the road to the Spawning Glen to devour the sporelings' spore sacs, and the husked remains of the mushrooms they once ate lie discarded across the ridge. The sporelings have always kept the bog lords at bay with spears and stones, but the giants have grown more aggressive, or more desperate, and no longer fear them.

title: The Spawning Glen
body: The Spawning Glen, west of the Cenarion Watchpost, is where young sporelings come from. Their spore sacs grow here, starting large and shrinking as the air inside them is spent, until only small, mature sacs remain. It is a fragile nursery, and it is under attack: starving fungal giants and bog lords wander through the glen devouring the sacs. The sporeling Fahssn keeps a desperate watch over them and begs any friendly outsider who passes to save as many as can be saved.

title: Sporeggar
body: Sporeggar is the village of the sporelings, a small and mostly peaceful people, on the western side of Zangarmarsh between Sporewind Lake and Marshlight Lake. It is grown from tallstalk mushrooms raised from fertile spores, and much of it has had to be regrown after attacks by the bog lords. Glowcap mushrooms serve the sporelings as coin. Their elder, Msshi'fn, welcomes outsiders who prove themselves, though others, like Gshaff, still cannot decide what to make of them. The village has enemies on every side: the bog lords, the marsh walkers of old, the spore giants of the Underbog and the Bloodscale naga to the northeast.

title: Marshlight Lake and Bloodscale Enclave
body: Marshlight Lake, in the west of the marsh, is the haunt of bogstroks, whose hatchlings swarm the shallows, and of a giant among them called Terrorclaw. On its shore the Bloodscale naga keep the Bloodscale Enclave and the Marshlight steam pump, worked by Wrekt slaves under the whips of slavedrivers and enchantresses. One naga taskmaster is said to amuse himself by sending slaves out to the lake's islands just when Terrorclaw is ready to feed. The enclave's naga have also been killing the sporelings of nearby Sporeggar, and they once kept their most prized possession here, the Ark of Ssslith, until a fungal giant carried it off.

title: Zabra'jin
body: Zabra'jin is the Darkspear town in the west of the marsh, overseen by Shadow Hunter Denjai, who commands the trolls' forces in Zangarmarsh. Witch Doctor Tor'gash reads omens in burstcap spores and keeps two pet murlocs, Gargle and Gurgle, while Seer Janidi says he need only ask the spirits. Gambarinka has given up rusting metal tools for the blades of marshfang slicers, Zurjaya is glad of fishing water after the wastes of Hellfire, and a captured gnome repairs gear under a guard who threatens to eat him. Yet the town is hemmed in by ogres cutting their way from the north and Daggerfen assassins on the roads, and a messenger from Garadar has come begging for help.

title: Daggerfen Village
body: Daggerfen Village lies in the northwest of the marsh, west of the Orebor Harborage. Its people, the Daggerfen, are the most cunning and aggressive of the marsh's Lost One tribes, a whole tribe of assassins who brew a potent poison from a ragveil base. They make no secret of wanting to rule the other Lost Ones, and under Chieftain Mummaki they have killed many scouts and messengers, Kurenai, draenei and troll alike, in a bid to seize the roads. Not everything here is grim: thanks to a mischievous Darkspear witch doctor, a few baby murlocs now splash among the huts.

title: Hewn Bog
body: The Hewn Bog, in the north of the marsh, has earned its name. Ango'rosh ogres have moved in and are chopping down its giant mushrooms, a cutting operation overseen by the brute Boss Grog'ak, and the felling threatens to cut a path to the walls of Zabra'jin. Ogres and their shamans now swarm where the mushroom forest stood. The harm reaches farther than it seems: the bog lords of Quagg Ridge once came here to feed, and with their food carried off by the ogres, they have turned on the sporelings' spawning grounds instead.

title: Ango'rosh Grounds and Stronghold
body: Northwest of Zabra'jin, the Ango'rosh ogres hold lands of their own. The Ango'rosh Grounds are an armed camp of brutes, maulers, warlocks and sentries under Captain Krosh and Captain Bo'kar, and plans for an attack on the troll town have been found there. Beyond the camp, a fallen mushroom bridges the water to a small floating island, and in a cave there lies the Ango'rosh Stronghold, stacked with boxes of harvested mushrooms and held by maulers, souleaters, shadowmages and Mal'druk the Soulrender. Its master is Overlord Gorefist, the leader who holds the whole tribe together.

title: Orebor Harborage
body: In the ruins of an old draenei temple northwest of Serpent Lake, a small band of Broken has made a home. These are the Kurenai, Broken who wish to reunite with their draenei kin, sent from their city of Telaar in Nagrand under Ikuti to strengthen ties with Telredor and keep the roads between them open. They are wary of strangers, for wariness has kept them alive. Puluu senses that the temple once meant something to him and hopes the draenei can help him remember. Maktu, once a slave, makes armor of fenclaw hide, and a human who likes to be called the specialist studies the poisons of the Lost Ones.

title: Serpent Lake and Bloodscale Grounds
body: Serpent Lake, in the north, lies at the heart of the naga's design. A hidden network of drains and pumps links the lakes of the region to it, and at its center a giant drain swallows the water of Zangarmarsh. On its eastern shore the Bloodscale naga hold the Bloodscale Grounds and the lake's own steam pump, where overseers, wavecallers and elementals drive Wrekt slaves under the command of the sorceress Rajis Fyashe. The deep water belongs to fenclaw thrashers, swarms of mudfin frenzies and Mragesh, an old and cunning hydra that has dogged many an angler and once nearly made a meal of a Kurenai hunter.

title: Coilfang Reservoir
body: Beneath Serpent Lake lies Coilfang Reservoir, the great pumping station of Lady Vashj, where the water drained from Zangarmarsh is gathered. Its entrance lies under the lake, where stone archways lead to the slave pens, the Underbog and the steam vaults of Warlord Kalithresh, and deeper still lies the Serpentshrine Cavern, where Vashj holds court. Orders bearing her seal have commanded that the Cenarion druids be slain on sight and the draining doubled. At the entrance, Watcher Jhang of the Expedition waits with a twisted ankle for word of four companions who went on inside, and Mortog Steamhead, saved by the Expedition from certain death in the mines, trades with the Expedition's friends.

title: Twin Spire Ruins
body: The Twin Spire Ruins stand near the middle of the marsh, the remains of a holy draenei site whose single broken tower, despite the name, still rises over an old burial ground. Both the Alliance and the Horde contest the surrounding marsh: each side strives to hold the two towers that watch over this part of Zangarmarsh and to raise its battle standard over the burial ground, and control passes back and forth as the fighting ebbs and flows. Around the ruins, mudfin frenzies thrash in the shallows and sporebats drift among the stones.

title: Ysiel Windsinger
body: Ysiel Windsinger, a night elf druid, leads the Cenarion Expedition from the Cenarion Refuge. The Expedition began as a small venture of the Cenarion Circle, but it has since grown large and largely independent, though she has not forgotten that it cannot exist without the Circle's support. She came to Outland expecting small pockets of life and found a thriving marsh, then watched its waters fall. Her magic can reshape a willing helper into a form suited to scouting the lakes from the air. When she learned that Lady Vashj stood behind the naga, she knew the Expedition's peaceful mission was over and began to prepare for war.

title: Morthis Whisperwing
body: Morthis Whisperwing is a former member of the Druids of the Talon, the old order that taught young druids the mysteries of flight before the druidic orders came together as the Cenarion Circle. The order is no more, but Morthis means to remain one of them to the end of his days, and he has long searched for an apprentice worthy of the secrets of the stormcrow. He is proud and particular, and pollen makes him sneeze, to his great indignity. He envies the freedom of his two birds, Rook and Corvax, and says he will take wing again once one last task is done.

title: Warden Hamoot
body: Warden Hamoot is in charge of the Cenarion Expedition's security. Ysiel brought wardens with her because she expected some opposition in Outland, but no one foresaw the strength and numbers of the naga, whose lethal attacks began the moment the Expedition set foot in the marsh. While the druids study plants and lakes, Hamoot deals with the hostiles. He pays out the Expedition's bounties on the leaders of the Bloodscale and the Darkcrest, pays for proof of victories over the naga, and has set his sights on the marsh beasts of Funggor Cavern. He never liked the naga of Azeroth, likes these even less, and sheds no tears for them.

title: Ikeyen
body: Ikeyen is a Broken who escaped slavery among the Umbrafen Lost Ones and found safety at the Cenarion Refuge. The druids protect him from the naga and the traitor tribes, and in return he teaches them about the plants and animals of the marsh. Old and weakened, he still lives in fear, certain that the Umbrafen would cut his throat if he left the Refuge for even a day. After his escape he hid in a cave south of their village, only to find it fought over by marsh beasts and spore men, and he had to flee again, leaving behind the few things he owned.

title: Anchorite Ahuurn
body: Anchorite Ahuurn leads Telredor. Once a cloistered priest of a quiet retreat, he opened its doors when the orcs fell upon his people and turned the shrine into a haven for refugees, and many draenei owe him their lives. He says Telredor has seen more change in twenty years than in the centuries before, and that the Light has brought him friends he could never have met in his cloister. He hopes to make Telredor a safe home for all who stand with the draenei, and has reached out to the Kurenai at the Orebor Harborage and even to the Lost Ones of the Feralfen, though they refused him.

title: Ikuti
body: Ikuti leads the Kurenai at the Orebor Harborage, a band of Broken sent from Telaar in Nagrand to strengthen ties with the draenei of Telredor. He greets visitors kindly but admits that wariness has often been all that stood between his people and death, and his trust must be earned. The Kurenai are content to help the Lost Ones who seek them out, yet unlike some draenei they will not go chasing after the rest, though they act quickly against tribes like the Daggerfen. Those who prove themselves to Ikuti are sent on to Telaar with his word, to his friend Nahuud, who counts Ikuti a brother.

title: Shadow Hunter Denjai
body: Shadow Hunter Denjai oversees Zabra'jin and commands the Darkspear forces in Zangarmarsh. He sent a crew east to build Swamprat Post and give the Horde a presence on the eastern border, and he expects regular reports, which some of his trolls find a trial. Denjai has reason to worry. The Ango'rosh ogres are cutting their way toward his walls and have drawn up plans to attack, while Daggerfen assassins pick off his scouts and messengers and threaten to surround the town. He has asked the orcs of Thunderlord Stronghold for aid, but they have ogre troubles of their own.

title: Msshi'fn
body: Msshi'fn is the elder of Sporeggar, called the Sporeggar Primus, and it falls to him to see that his people have what they need. He welcomes outsiders who prove their friendship, even though few of their kind ever come to Sporeggar, and he receives with gratitude the rescued spore sacs that carry the next generation of sporelings. Like the rest of his people he deals in glowcap mushrooms, which the sporelings use as coin, and he will teach a trusted friend how to pick them from the ground without ruining them.

title: Fhwoor
body: Fhwoor is a fungal giant who lives among the sporelings of Sporeggar, an odd sight given how much grief the other giants of the marsh cause them. The sporelings rescued him from the naga some time ago, and he has stayed with them ever since, helping with whatever needs doing. He speaks simply: he likes the little sporelings, because they saved him, he does not eat them, and he hates the naga. When the Bloodscale began killing sporelings, Fhwoor marched into their village by the Marshlight steam pump and carried off their most prized possession, the Ark of Ssslith.

title: Rajis Fyashe
body: Rajis Fyashe is a naga sorceress and the leader of the Bloodscale, the naga who guard steam pumps at Serpent Lake and Marshlight Lake and drive Wrekt slaves at the work. Her people have attacked the Expedition's scouts and killed the sporelings of Sporeggar. The Cenarion Expedition has declared a bounty on her, warning that the Bloodscale are extremely dangerous and that their leader must be approached with the greatest caution. She was last sighted at Serpent Lake, among her overseers and wavecallers on the Bloodscale Grounds.

title: Balance Must Be Preserved
body: When the Cenarion Expedition began taking measurements in the marsh, it found the water in the lakes falling steadily, a change that threatened every plant and creature in Zangarmarsh. Ysiel Windsinger sent a helper to Umbrafen Lake to find the cause, and the answer was a steam pump on the shore, worked by naga. That explained the naga's open hostility toward the druids, but not how far their work reached. Ysiel reshaped her helper with a stormcrow amulet and sent them winging over every great lake, and the flight revealed pumping stations at all of them. She then handed over seeds carrying the rage of the earth, to be sown on the controls of the pumps at Umbrafen Lake, Serpent Lake, Marshlight Lake and the Lagoon. Vines as thick as an arm and as strong as iron choked the machines. The marsh was saved for now, Ysiel said, but this would not be the last of the naga.

title: The Drain Beneath Serpent Lake
body: Schematics taken from the naga showed a hidden network of drains and pumps linking the lakes of the region to Serpent Lake, with a giant drain at its center, and a search of the lake proved them right: the naga had made it a sink for all of Zangarmarsh. Ysiel sent a team of druids to investigate the drain and sent word to the Circle's emissaries at Cenarion Post in Hellfire Peninsula, but the Circle could promise help only when possible, its members tied up in Moonglade and Silithus. The druid team never came back. Watcher Jhang was found hiding at the entrance to Coilfang Reservoir with a twisted ankle, while the others had gone on into the slave pens and the Underbog. Jhang had seen naga pass through an archway into the steam vaults, speaking the name of Warlord Kalithresh. Then orders came to light bearing the seal of Lady Vashj herself, and Ysiel knew the Expedition was at war.

title: The Bog Lords' Hunger
body: At the Cenarion Watchpost, Watcher Leesa'oh set out to learn how the sporelings live alongside the creatures around them, and a survey of the Spawning Glen revealed something alarming: the bog lords of Quagg Ridge were crossing the road to eat the sporelings' spore sacs. The giants were starving. Husked mushroom remains found on the ridge matched a kind Leesa'oh had seen elsewhere, and samples from the Hewn Bog confirmed it: Ango'rosh ogres had moved in and were cutting down the mushrooms the bog lords fed on. Leesa'oh would not hear of wiping out the ogres, who had as much right to the marsh as anyone. Instead she had boxes of harvested mushrooms taken back from the Ango'rosh Stronghold and planted them by her camp, with Buddy the cat looking on, to grow the giants a new garden. It worked, sparing the sporelings from the bog lords, and the bog lords from the Expedition's wrath.

title: The Sporelings' Plight
body: At the Spawning Glen, the sporeling Fahssn begged passing strangers for help. Fungal giants were devouring the spore sacs from which young sporelings come, and the bog lords no longer feared sporeling spears and stones. Those who saved the sacs and fought off the giants were sent on to Sporeggar with the rescued sacs for the elder Msshi'fn, and were welcomed into the sporelings' homes. Sporeggar had other troubles. Its tallstalks needed regrowing after the bog lord attacks, its old enemies the marsh walkers had to be held off, and the Bloodscale naga to the northeast had begun killing sporelings. Fhwoor, the friendly fungal giant, marched into the naga village by the Marshlight pump and carried off the Ark of Ssslith, in the hope that the naga would take the hint and return to their reservoir. Meanwhile the sporelings wage a war of their own against the spore giants of the Underbog, for, as they say, all is fair in mushrooms and war.

title: Spirits of the Feralfen
body: Anchorite Ahuurn of Telredor hoped to redeem the Lost Ones, and the Feralfen seemed a promising start, for they had settled in the old draenei temple of Boha'mu as if remembering something of their past. Their idols showed a fixation on birds, though no birds live in the marsh, and Ahuurn guessed they had met the arakkoa and taken them for bird spirits. He brewed a potion to lend his envoy the shape of an arakkoa, and in that guise the envoy greeted Elder Kuruti. The elder saw through it. His people wanted nothing from the draenei who had turned their backs on them, he said, least of all a redemption offered through trickery. At Zabra'jin, Seer Janidi studied the same totems for his own reasons. Scorning the bird, he coveted the serpent spirit's power, but when his totem was planted at the foot of the temple stairs the serpent rose and attacked, loyal to the Feralfen.

title: The Withering of the Dead Mire
body: At Telredor, Vindicator Idaar noticed that life in the land to the northeast was withering without any clear cause. A soil sample from what came to be called the Dead Mire was nearly dry, and the fungal giants there, maddened by their pain, were beyond saving, so the kindest course was to end their suffering. A withered basidium taken from one of the giants told more. Ruam at Telredor and Reavij at Swamprat Post each recognized it: the Dead Mire had once been a lake and the giants' spawning ground, and with the water gone they could no longer spore. Samples from parched hydras and withered bog lords showed the drought taking its toll on creatures never meant to live dry. The Horde learned the cost firsthand. Scout Jyoba of Swamprat Post went into the mire and never returned, and his body was found beside his spilled ink, his report in the hands of the withered giants that had killed him.

title: The Ango'rosh Threat
body: The Ango'rosh ogres have long been filtering down from the northern mountains, and now they threaten both sides of the marsh. At Zabra'jin a wanted poster called for the head of Boss Grog'ak, who ran the mushroom cutting north of the town, and Shadow Hunter Denjai suspected its position was no accident. Plans found at the Ango'rosh Grounds proved him right: the ogres were preparing an attack. At the Orebor Harborage, Ikuti watched the same ogres strip the Hewn Bog and creep toward the Kurenai temple. Both sides reached the same answer. The Ango'rosh Stronghold lies in a cave on a small island across a fallen mushroom, and there Overlord Gorefist was slain among his maulers. Ikuti knew a tribe without its leader would fall to fighting over who rules next, while Denjai wondered aloud how long it would be before the brutes found another bloodthirsty chieftain.

title: The Raven God
body: Morthis Whisperwing, once of the Druids of the Talon, accepts a druid as his apprentice in the secrets of the stormcrow. The relics of that training lie with Clintar Dreamwalker, asleep in the barrow dens of Moonglade, so Morthis brews a Ward of Waking from common herbs, moonwell water and the fragile bogblossoms atop the tallest mushrooms. With a fragment of Clintar's spirit as guide the relics are recovered, but in the dens a raven is seen. That sign sends the apprentice to Arthorn Windsong at the Evergrove in Blade's Edge, who studies an arakkoa cult of a raven god. Its scripture, the Book of the Raven, is pieced together from stones buried near Skettis and gives the god's name, Anzu, and the shrines where his followers bound his rivals, from which the apprentice recovers the essences of the eagle, falcon and hawk. Morthis binds the essences into a Southfury moonstone from Azshara, and in the Sethekk Halls the stone lures Anzu out of the Dream to be defeated. Morthis bids his student keep it, lest Anzu return.
